rules.term_types: every skill declares two search-term fields: keywords (canonical searchable terms, required and non-empty) and aliases (alternate spellings and abbreviations, may be empty); both are matched with the same boundary-safe rules, keywords are iterated before aliases, and a term is unique across the whole taxonomy (keywords and aliases alike are rejected at load time if duplicated)
rules.case_handling: matching is case-insensitive: the term and the searched text are both casefolded before matching
rules.boundary_matching: terms match only at word boundaries ((?<!\w) term (?!\w) on the casefolded text); a term never matches inside a larger word, so 'java' cannot match 'javascript', 'ml' cannot match 'html'/'similar', and 'git' cannot match 'github'
rules.connector_variants: whitespace, '-', '_' and '/' between the words of a multi-word term are interchangeable, so 'machine learning' matches 'machine-learning' and 'machine_learning'; punctuation inside a single-token term (C++, C#, n8n) is matched literally, and versioned spellings such as 'C++17' are deliberately not matched in 0.1.0
rules.fields_searched: title_raw, excerpt_raw, categories_raw (joined with spaces), description_html_raw (converted to visible text); searched in that fixed order
rules.html_handling: description_html_raw is converted to visible text for matching only (tags stripped, HTML entities unescaped, whitespace collapsed); the raw field is never modified
rules.evidence_behavior: one evidence entry per (field, matched term) recording the term, its type (keyword or alias), the first-occurrence excerpt, and an occurrence count; a skill is listed at most once per record; evidence is ordered by searched-field order, then taxonomy definition order (keywords before aliases)
rules.deduplication: duplicate terms — keywords or aliases — are rejected at taxonomy load time (fail-closed); duplicate occurrences of the same term in one field collapse into one evidence entry with occurrence_count
rules.missing_fields: missing or empty fields are skipped and reported in skipped_fields; they are never coerced into evidence
rules.no_match: a record without any match is represented as evidence_status 'no_evidence' with an empty skills list; no_evidence is not evidence of absence
rules.negation: 0.1.0 does not parse negation or context (for example 'no prior experience in AI is required' still matches 'ai'); a match is keyword evidence only

excluded_terms.go: excluded: word-boundary matching cannot distinguish the Go language from the common English verb 'go'
excluded_terms.r: excluded: a single-letter alias would be unsafe under boundary matching
excluded_terms.js: excluded: over-broad standalone abbreviation; 'javascript' is matched instead
excluded_terms.ts: excluded: over-broad standalone abbreviation; 'typescript' is matched instead
excluded_terms.sql: reserved: not evidenced in the 20-record development sample; may be added in a later taxonomy version
